channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Data-Center Firm Elice Plunges 32% in Debut After Korea IPO
item.description: Data-center infrastructure company Elice Inc. plunged in its trading debut on South Korea’s tech-heavy Kosdaq market after raising 201 billion won ($151 million) in the bourse’s biggest initial public offering this year.
item.dc:creator: Yoolim Lee and Youkyung Lee

item.title: CATL’s Valuation Gap Highlights Investor Divide as Earnings Near
item.description: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd.’s Hong Kong-listed shares have maintained a considerable premium over their Shenzhen-traded peers after a months-long selloff, underscoring a divide between onshore and offshore investors ahead of the Chinese battery giant’s earnings release.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Z.AI Founders Worked on Research Funded by China Institute UK Tied to Spies
item.description: Four founders of one of China’s most promising artificial intelligence companies, Z.AI Co., worked on research in a joint project with a technology institute that the UK government accused of having “very strong ties” to China’s main spy agency, according to publicly available research papers from China and an “espionage alert” from the UK.
item.dc:creator: Kate O'Keeffe and Maggie Eastland

item.title: Alger’s Crawford: There’s Skittishness in the Market
item.description: Ankur Crawford, a Portfolio Manager at Alger and Former Intel Engineer, said recent market nervousness around AI— including concerns tied to CoreWeave—does not reflect the strength of underlying adoption and infrastructure demand. She described a striking gap between stock performance and on-the-ground fundamentals, while noting that returns from AI investment will take time and that debt, supply-chain bottlenecks, labor shortages and power constraints could slow the buildout. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Take: CoreWeave And The Fragile AI Economy
item.description: CoreWeave’s debt is rattling some investors. Today on the Big Take podcast, what the company’s financial strain reveals about the AI boom and what lies ahead for cloud infrastructure providers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Tech Earnings Could Validate AI, Ives Says
item.description: Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville, Ives, and Company, says the upcoming earnings from major technology companies will be an important test of confidence in AI. He also talks about giving investors a chance to invest in private ai companies. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tenstorrent CEO on New Funding Round, AI Progress
item.description: Tenstorrent CEO Jim Keller discussed the chip startup’s $1.5 billion funding round, which values the company at about $6.2 billion. He said the company is focused on scaling its Galaxy server program and developing AI intellectual property, rather than pursuing a sale. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Bailey Lipschultz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Retailers Will Struggle During Earnings Season, Says Meredith Whitney
item.description: Meredith Whitney, CEO of the Meredith Whitney Advisory Group, says many retailers will struggle during this earnings season because because household costs have been rising since the start of the Iran war. She speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Eric Schmidt’s 1% Anthropic Stake Set to Pay Massive Windfall
item.description: Former Google Chief Executive Officer Eric Schmidt owns around 1% of Anthropic PBC thanks to his early investment in the startup, according to people familiar with the matter, setting him up for one of the largest individual windfalls from the company’s imminent public market debut.
item.dc:creator: Natasha Mascarenhas and Tom Maloney

item.title: JPMorgan's 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions
item.description: David Kelly, chief global strategist at JPMorgan Asset Management, and Stephen Parker, co-head of global investment strategy at JPMorgan Private Bank, discuss their latest Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions report, which projects about 7% annual returns for 60/40 portfolios over the next 10–15 years. They speak on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: FTC Requires Publicis to Offer Equal Access to LiveRamp Data
item.description: The US Federal Trade Commission said it will allow Publicis Groupe SA to complete the $2.2 billion acquisition of LiveRamp Holdings Inc. if the French media giant agrees to offer equal access to the digital advertising platform’s data connectivity services to rivals.
item.dc:creator: Leah Nylen

item.title: Intel Asks FCC to Allow Upgrades for Banned Foreign Robots
item.description: Intel Corp. asked the Federal Communications Commission to make an exception to a recent ban on foreign-made advanced robotics, telling the agency it needs continued access to “niche” equipment critical to US semiconductor manufacturing.
item.dc:creator: Kelcee Griffis and Ian King

item.title: Goldman's Lynam Isn't Worried About Access to Debt Amid AI Buildout
item.description: Amanda Lynam, chief credit strategist at Goldman Sachs, says recent widening in AI-related credit spreads resembles an earlier episode but differs because high-yield debt is now leading the move and investors are raising fundamental questions. She speaks on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Japan Launches Probe in First Sampling Mission to a Moon of Mars
item.description: Japan launched a probe bound for a moon of Mars, giving the nation a head start over China in the race to become the first to return samples from the Red Planet or one of its moons.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Takahashi

item.title: Nscale, Anthropic in Talks for $45 Billion Cloud Computing Deal
item.description: Nscale Ltd., the AI cloud computing firm, is in talks to sell computing power to Anthropic PBC in a deal that could be worth about $45 billion, according to people familiar with the negotiations.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz, Dina Bass and Brody Ford

item.title: AI Firm Nscale Faces Investor Pushback Over IPO Valuation
item.description: Bloomberg's Brody Ford said that issues facing the IPO of AI firm Nscale are 'endemic' to the larger AI data center industry as developers try to source power and labor and contend with potential delays. Bloomberg's Bailey Lipschultz said that the tone has shifted for AI IPOs as more companies slow down on going public before the end of the year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: OpenAI Staffer Charged With Bugging Office Stays Jailed for Now
item.description: The OpenAI software engineer charged with planting a hidden recording device in one of the company’s offices must remain in jail for the time being, a federal judge ruled.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Metz and Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Tech Stocks Pull S&P 500 Higher as Opportunistic Buyers Step In
item.description: Chips companies rallied in Monday trading, helping stocks rebound after the worst week for the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index since the tariff turmoil of April 2025.
item.dc:creator: Felice Maranz

item.title: Vinted Cracks Down on Looted Goods After French Riots
item.description: Vinted, a secondhand online marketplace that counts France as one of its largest markets, has seen an influx of listings suspected to contain looted items after riots broke out across the country.
item.dc:creator: Yazhou Sun

item.title: Musk Plans to Gift SpaceX Shares to Kids Through Trump Accounts
item.description: Elon Musk vowed to distribute a share of SpaceX to each child in the US, a multibillion-dollar pledge that adds to a string of sizable donations from the tech industry for the benefit of the American public.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen and Ed Ludlow
